sections.h2: Which Cherokee County office sends the bill, and which one sets the value?
sections.html:
Cherokee County splits the work between two offices on the same stretch of Marietta Highway in Canton. The Tax Commissioner handles real estate, personal property, public utility, timber, motor vehicle and mobile home taxes, then distributes the collections to state, county, school and city governments. The Tax Assessors' Office decides what your property is worth and which exemptions you receive.

  • Tax Commissioner: 678-493-6400, cherokeecountytax.com. Main office at 2780 Marietta Hwy, Canton, and an annex at 155 Towne Lake Pkwy, Woodstock, both open 8:00am to 5:00pm Monday through Friday.
  • Tax Assessors' Office: 678-493-6120, 2782 Marietta Hwy, Suite 200, Canton. Returns are filed here during the season that ends April 1.
  • City tax offices bill separately inside Ball Ground, Canton, Holly Springs, Mountain Park, Nelson, Waleska and Woodstock, so check whether your address is incorporated.

Cherokee County's Assessors Office posts a public notice that appraisal staff may visit a property after an appeal, a new return, new construction or a conservation use application. The visiting appraisers carry county photo identification and drive marked county vehicles, and answering their questions is voluntary.

sections.h2: What do sellers in Cherokee County, Georgia need to know about the county?
sections.html:
Cherokee County was created by the General Assembly on December 26, 1831, and Canton became the seat after the early county seat of Etowah was renamed. Growth took off after the first phase of Interstate 575 opened in 1979. The freeway bisects the county from Kennesaw through Woodstock, Holly Springs and Canton to Ball Ground, and the southern end nearest Atlanta is the most densely settled.

The county covers 434 square miles, of which 422 are land. Lake Allatoona fills much of the southwest corner, and the north climbs toward the foothills, with Bear Mountain at 2,297 feet the highest listed summit. Reinhardt University is in Waleska, Chattahoochee Technical College has campuses in Woodstock and Canton, and one school district, the Cherokee County School District, serves every address.

QuickFacts counts 299,273 residents for 2025, which is 12.2% above the 2020 base. Its 2020 to 2024 figures give $435,100 as the middle value of an owner-held house, $108,115 as the middle household income and 77.3% as the owner-occupancy rate. Commutes average 31.3 minutes, and builders pulled 1,524 permits in 2025.

sections.h2: What is the Cherokee County due date for property tax?
sections.html:
Bills go out in September and the payment is due November 15. Whatever remains unpaid after that is delinquent, and the Tax Commissioner reminds owners that a lien then attaches to the property. Mobile home bills are mailed each January with an April 1 deadline.

The county's 2026 rates, as the Tax Commissioner prints them, are in the table. One mill equals a dollar for each thousand dollars of assessed value, and assessed value is 40% of market value in Georgia.

sections.h2: How can an owner challenge a Cherokee County value?
sections.html:
Put your appeal in writing and deliver it to the assessors inside the 45 day period that starts when the assessment notice is mailed. The state's uniform form asks you to choose a Board of Equalization hearing, a hearing officer or arbitration, and the grounds may be taxability, value, uniformity or a denied exemption.

The county appraisal staff values property with sales comparison, cost and income approaches and tests the results statistically by area, neighborhood and class of property. A good appeal answers those methods with your own evidence.

  • Recent closed sales of similar houses nearby, with dates and prices.
  • Photos and repair estimates that show condition problems the record may not reflect.
  • A copy of your settlement statement or warranty deed if you bought the property recently.

Complaints about the size of the tax are outside an appeal, because assessors do not set millage rates. The governing bodies named on your bill do that.

sections.h2: Where does a Cherokee County owner apply for a homestead exemption?
sections.html:
Apply in person at the Tax Assessors' Office with a valid Georgia driver's license or ID showing the current address of the property. Bring your settlement statement or warranty deed too, since staff print and complete the application when you arrive.

The state's standard homestead exemption applies to an owner-occupied primary residence, and the county can add to it. State revenue guidance adds that an application is taken all year but must be in by April 1 to count for that tax year, and that skipping the application waives the exemption. Ask the Assessors' Office which Cherokee County exemptions for seniors, disabled veterans or surviving spouses fit your situation, since the amounts change.

An exemption follows the person who applied, so a buyer starts over with a new application.

sections.h2: What does selling do to a Cherokee County tax bill?
sections.html:
Georgia taxes whoever holds title on New Year's Day, and the Cherokee County Tax Commissioner says the law gives its office no way to prorate tax for part of a year. The buyer and seller must agree on any split when they close.

A buyer who closes in the fall will not automatically receive a bill. The Tax Commissioner asks to receive the closing statement so the bill can be reissued in the new owner's name, which works for purchases completed before November 15 of that tax year. Should October 1 pass with no bill in hand, phone 678-493-6400 or print one from the website. Even when the bill stays in the seller's name, the lien follows the property if it turns delinquent.

A properly completed PT-61 transfer form on file at the Superior Court clerk's office can stand in for a new real property return in the sale year, as long as nothing was subdivided or built.

sections.h2: What happens when Cherokee County property goes to a tax sale?
sections.html:
A tax sale buyer gets a tax deed but cannot move in, build, or remove tenants right away. The owner, a creditor or any other interested party can buy the property back within 12 months.

The redemption price is the bid, plus taxes the buyer paid afterward, plus special assessments, plus a premium of 20% of the amount for the first year or part of a year and 10% for each year after that, plus sheriff and advertising costs. After 12 months the buyer may serve a notice of foreclosure of the right to redeem by certified mail to the recorded owner and each interest holder, and the notice must also be printed weekly for four straight weeks in the county newspaper.

Should an auction bring in more than is owed, the the surplus is held separately, and O.C.G.A. 48-4-5 lets the owner of record at that time, plus security deed holders, claim it. The county adds that claimants are not required to pay or hire any third party.

faqs.q: When must a Cherokee County bill be paid?
faqs.a: November 15. Bills are mailed in September, and taxes not paid by that date are considered delinquent.

faqs.q: Will the Cherokee County Tax Commissioner prorate at a sale?
faqs.a: No. The office has no legal provision for prorating partial-year ownership, so any split is settled by the parties at closing.

faqs.q: Where can I file for homestead in Cherokee County?
faqs.a: File in person at the Tax Assessors' Office, 2782 Marietta Hwy, Suite 200, Canton, with a Georgia license or ID showing the property address.

faqs.q: How long can an owner redeem after a tax sale?
faqs.a: Twelve months from the sale date. After that the buyer may start the foreclosure of the right to redeem by sending notice.

faqs.q: How can I find my Cherokee County tax bill if I did not receive one?
faqs.a: Call the Tax Commissioner at 678-493-6400 or print a copy from cherokeecountytax.com. The office suggests doing so if a bill has not arrived by October 1.
